summary: R0 (dim=8, k=128, 0.875 nominal BPW) is at or extremely near the practical ceiling gravity-pq (S=1, power-of-2 dim) can reach for GLM-5.2's real tensor sizes. No candidate strictly between 0.875 and BPW_CEILING=1.0 is admissible across the T1-tier size range.

how_found.step_1: Attempted rung R1 (dim=11, k=1024, nominal 0.909) to test routed_expert (97.5% of mass) at a rate between R0 and general-v1's literal T1=1.0bpw target.
how_found.step_2: R1 packing produced nonsensical per-tensor BPW (0.17-0.45, varying inversely with tensor size) with no error raised.
how_found.step_3: Root cause: gravity_forge._pq_geometry() requires dim to be a power of 2; dim=11 silently falls back to _largest_pow2_divisor(cols) instead of raising. R1 was never packed at its requested rate.
how_found.step_4: Corrected search over every (dim, k) with dim in {8,16,32,64,128}, checked for admissibility at GLM-5.2's real T1 sizes (routed_expert 12,582,912; dense_mlp up to 75,497,472; attention as small as 3,538,944 elements): zero candidates strictly above R0's 0.875 and below 1.0 pass admissibility across that range.

implication: general-v1's tier_rates T1=num8/den8=1.0bpw is not reachable by the gravity-pq codec for routed_expert/shared_expert/attention/dense_mlp tensors at GLM-5.2's scale, regardless of Prometheus conditioning. Reaching it would require crossing BPW_CEILING=1.0, which needs a formal Escape Receipt -- a deliberate reversal of this project's sub-bit-first LAW (see hawking_gravity_subbit_law_2026_07_17 in memory), not invoked here.
consequence: Bracketing upward via a new PQ rung, as HAWKING_MOTHERLOAD_COMPLETION_CAMPAIGN.md §3.3 describes (H10/H12/H15), is not achievable within the current codec architecture for a uniform or near-uniform routed_expert rate. The only levers that remain inside the sub-bit LAW are (a) protecting MORE tensors natively (expensive: 16bpw vs 0.875, ~18x bytes for whatever fraction moves), which was already tried for the two worst-reconstructing tensors and did not fix the collapse, or (b) a fundamentally different, non-PQ codec, which is out of scope for this campaign. Formally invoking the Escape Receipt is a policy decision, not an engineering one, and needs explicit authorization.

correction_2.what: The prior consequence field called crossing BPW_CEILING an Escape Receipt that could be formally invoked with authorization. That was wrong. tools/foundry/one_bit_ceiling.py enforces the ceiling in code, not prose: target_bpw > 1 is REJECTED with the literal message no automatic Escape Receipt as one of several forbidden overrides (alongside 1.2/1.5/2.0/3.0 anchors). There is no escape mechanism to invoke -- the phrase names something that does not exist, not a gate that does.
correction_2.law_text: Hawking does not climb above one bit to discover where conventional quantization works. Hawking changes the representation, model, allocation and treatment until useful intelligence survives at one bit or below.
correction_2.implication: M03 is terminal under this project own binding rules, not merely terminal within one codec family by choice. Going above 1.0 BPW is not available under any authorization. The only legal remaining levers are a different representation/allocation entirely (out of scope here; project history -- Gravity Forge sub-bit foundry, Second Light, Sub-Bit Readiness Diagnostic -- shows repeated prior negative results attempting exactly this at other model scales) or accepting R0 as the sealed floor per the HONEST_EMPIRICAL_FLOOR precedent this project has used before.
